name: Mod-owned crane cache in opaque savestate metadata
scope: Restores the original RNG rolls and captured retail rotation speed which live outside the retail heap snapshot. Native actors are restored by the existing codec.

placement.container: Ghost::SavestateData (128 native u32 words, unchanged512 bytes)

payload.words2_to16: Five fixed-order triples: actor address, captured retail-speed f32 bits (zero if uncaptured), roll | (speedCaptured <<16). Empty triples are canonical zero.
payload.word17: FNV1a of preceding68 bytes; existing StoredState.metadataTag also covers the entire Ghost metadata block.

validation: Before any game memory restore: tag/schema/hash/reserved bits/empty rows/bounded aligned pointers/finite captured speed. No actor dereference.

After heap restore: verify all nonempty actors against expected region-specific vtable, name and key, then replace all five cache rows atomically. Any rejection clears every row, preventing reuse of a later reset cache.
Control wrappers and retail rand call counts are unchanged. No RNG roll is reconstructed from a customized native speed.

legacy.zero_or_sgpf_tail_zero: Remains structurally readable. Native actors remain untouched and unknown mod caches clear.
legacy.ricco_manual_ram: Valid practice RAM restores immediately; recording continuation is unavailable and the user is told to reset for crane controls.
legacy.ricco_direct_or_sd: Refuse missing controller metadata before copying rather than claim precise controller restoration. The archived file is preserved.
legacy.other_scenes: Missing crane metadata is harmless outside the crane scene.
legacy.older_builds: Older zero-prefix readers reject the nonzero optional tail. Older SGPF readers may ignore historically unused padding, so do not claim old implementations apply the new cache.

reason: A native Ricco replay isolated one actor whose rotating speed was restored from snapshotA then overwritten with cached resetB values. Restoring this cache fixes source gameplay state; replay witness validation remains strict.
tests: Native manual RAM capture -> reset -> restore -> full WorldWatch
